# notavibe

> Ranks open-source JavaScript, TypeScript and Python projects published to npm
> and PyPI on maintenance, not popularity. Five sourced signals per project — release
> cadence, contributor breadth, adoption, maintainer responses, and security
> posture — each shown as a named band with its data source and fetch date. No
> composite score. Exposed as an MCP server so coding assistants can ground
> dependency recommendations in real data.

## Site

- [Home](https://notavibe.dev/): what notavibe measures, the five signals, and how to connect the MCP server
- [Methodology](https://notavibe.dev/methodology): which packages are listed and how they are screened, what each signal measures, every band's cut-point, and how ranking works. This page is the source of truth for the rules summarised here
- [Privacy policy](https://notavibe.dev/privacy/): what personal data the site handles, why, who processes it, and GDPR rights

## Sections on the home page

- [Five signals, fully sourced, no black box](https://notavibe.dev/#how-it-works): the five maintenance signals and why each is reported as a band with its source and fetch date rather than a score
- [Connect the MCP server](https://notavibe.dev/#install): a hosted remote MCP server at `https://notavibe.dev/mcp` (streamable HTTP, no API key); set up by URL, with a Claude Code command, or with a JSON config
- [Built for the questions your tooling doesn't answer](https://notavibe.dev/#why): what notavibe is for, and what it deliberately is not

## Reference

- MCP server: `https://notavibe.dev/mcp` (HTTP). Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http notavibe https://notavibe.dev/mcp`
- MCP tools (none of them changes the catalog):
  - `search_projects`: search the catalog by words and exact filters
  - `get_project`: one project's public profile, by repository or by npm or PyPI package name
  - `compare_projects`: two projects' public profiles side by side, with no winner named
  - `get_lists`: the public curated lists, or the members of one list
  - `get_methodology`: what each signal measures, with its bands and cut-points, from the same source as the methodology page
  - `check_dependencies`: look up to 100 npm or PyPI package names in one call and get one row per name
  - `get_more_tools`: tell the maintainers about a capability the other tools are missing

## Notes for agents

- notavibe reports maintenance signals, not security vulnerabilities. It is not a CVE scanner.
- Every signal is a named band carrying its own source and fetch date. There is no single composite score, and inventing one misrepresents the product.
- "Insufficient data" is a valid answer and is reported as such rather than guessed.
- The catalog currently covers two ecosystems: JavaScript and TypeScript, from npm, and Python, from PyPI. Its coverage of each is partial: it does not yet hold every JavaScript or TypeScript project published to npm, or every Python project published to PyPI.
- New packages come from the npm and PyPI registries' feeds. A project without a package can be requested.
- A package's data counts only when the package and its repository name each other: the repository's package.json names the npm package, or its root pyproject.toml names the PyPI package, and the package names the repository as its source, or a verified signed publish attestation names the repository. A package's own claim is never enough on its own.
- Every package is screened against OpenSSF Malicious Packages reports on OSV before it is listed, and checked again when a report changes. A package with a report on another of its releases waits for a staff review. This screen keeps known-malicious packages out; it is not a vulnerability scan.
